frequency_question: How often do besieged nations successfully stand up domestic manufacturing lines for complex foreign cruise missiles within two years?
membership_rule: Includes any sovereign state initiating domestic assembly or component manufacturing of a foreign-designed long-range cruise missile during an active high-intensity conflict. Excludes simple licensed production of small arms, artillery shells, or basic unguided rockets.

cases.name: Taiwan Hsiung Feng III domestic anti-ship missile scaling under perpetual threat
Ukraine Neptune missile rapid domestic production and deployment initiative
Iran domestic production of Soumar/Qods cruise missiles based on foreign blueprints

provenance_note: 3 cases named, 5 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.7x)
coverage_note: 3 named; believed roughly 5 in total matching the high-complexity wartime transfer filter
known_gaps: Extremely classified nature of missile technology transfers limits public dataset visibility.
skeleton: State-level defense localization efforts for complex missiles divided into high-tech transfers versus indigenous iterations
multiplier: 3 hits out of 5 relevant major historical precedents
validity_reason: Industrial base dynamics and technology transfer security protocols evolve slowly over multi-year periods.
